paper.title_en: From Binary Wind to Radio Burst: Dispersion-Measure Evolution after Accretion-induced Collapse
paper.abstract_en: Secular changes in the dispersion measures (DMs) of repeating fast radio bursts probe the source-local plasma. Such DM time variability has been interpreted with spherical, single-density-profile models. Accretion-induced collapse (AIC) of a white dwarf may instead follow binary interaction and occur inside a finite, anisotropic circumstellar structure. Here, we construct an angle-dependent toy model of aspherical AIC ejecta propagating through a pre-AIC free wind, shocked-wind bubble, swept-up external shell, and polar cavity, exploring a diffuse environment (number density of $1~{\rm cm^{-3}}$, located at $10~$pc) and a compact cloud (number density of $500~{\rm cm^{-3}}$, located at $0.3~$pc), bracketing ionized and initially neutral upstream gas. The unshocked ejecta initially yield ${\rm DM}\propto t^{-2}$, while crossings of the finite wind-bubble interfaces produce breaks and curvature in ${\rm DM}(t)$. In initially neutral models, shock ionization can overcome geometric dilution: the total DM reverses from decline to growth after approximately $10$--$20$ yr and later turns over as the finite reservoir is processed. Ionized-upstream models instead generally decline or flatten. Without fitting individual sources, our models span both signs and the approximate magnitudes of the secular DM-variation rates measured among repeaters. In this dynamical framework, DM evolution is set by shock propagation through the circumsource density and ionization structure, rather than the contemporaneous burst rate, distinguishing it from photoionization-driven scenarios. Consequently, in our model, an instantaneous \(d{\rm DM}/dt\) is not a unique indicator of source age. We suggest that the observed distribution of secular DM variation slope amplitudes and signs will be important for distinguishing among different models of DM variations in repeating FRBs.
